items.title: Bitcoin keeps getting rejected at $87,000 as stocks hover near records
items.description: BTC fell back to about $85,600 after sellers turned it away from $87,000 for the third time since Sept. 23, while Nasdaq closed at a record and Treasury yields kept climbing.

items.description: Solana Foundation launched an open-source program that lets institutions settle trades in seconds, not days. JPMorgan provided key inputs.

items.description: The planned 24/7 venue will offer dozens of tokenized U.S. stocks, with trades conducted against stablecoins through blockchain-based liquidity pools rather than a traditional order book.

items.title: U.S. CFTC joins SEC in proposing crypto regulations, though spot-market gap lingers
items.description: The derivatives regulator is proposing two rules meant to cover the waterfront of crypto activity and exchanges, as long as it's not simple, direct trading.

items.title: Stripe to expand stablecoin cards to over 100 countries by the end of the year
items.description: The payments giant is planning a major global expansion for its stablecoin cards business, and is exploring tokenized deposits and DeFi use cases, new crypto head Henri Stern said.

items.title: Rain seeks US trust bank charter days after OCC sued over crypto charters
items.description: Rain joins a growing queue of crypto firms seeking federal trust charters, while community banks have just asked a court to overturn the OCC rules underpinning them.

items.title: OKX eyes emerging markets with yield-offering stablecoin savings and payments app
items.description: OKX Money lets users hold, send and spend dollar-backed stablecoins, with qualifying USDG balances earning up to 10% APY.

items.title: Chinese crime network laundered over $1B for Lazarus: ZachXBT
items.description: ZachXBT says he infiltrated the network by posing as a customer, gaining information that helped trace funds from the $1.5 billion Bybit hack.

items.title: Crypto PAC announces support for 32 House candidates in US midterms
items.description: Fairshake said it would financially back 32 House candidates who all voted in favor of the CLARITY market structure bill in 2025, as the legislation remains in limbo in the Senate.

items.title: FinCEN withdraws proposed crypto mixing rule over ‘legitimate activity’ concerns
items.description: The bureau under the US Treasury said it was withdrawing two proposed rules on unhosted wallets and crypto mixers ”as part of the Trump Administration’s deregulatory agenda.”

items.title: Modern Treasury seeks US trust bank charter for digital asset custody
items.description: The payments infrastructure company is seeking federal approval to offer stablecoin custody and related fiat services through a limited-purpose national trust bank.

items.title: Advocacy group pushes back on banks’ lawsuit against OCC over charters
items.description: CCI CEO Ji Hun Kim said that the organization “remains confident“ in the OCC’s approval of charters for crypto companies, despite a recent lawsuit and pushback from some lawmakers.

items.title: S&P Global brings risk assessments to growing crypto lending vault sector
items.description: S&P Global’s new framework evaluates digital asset lending vaults across six risk categories as deposits in the sector climb to about $10 billion.

items.title: Trump offers U.S. help to Russia after plague death; WHO assesses the situation as low risk
items.description: WHO said it was in contact with Russian authorities, and has offered support if needed, while assessing the risk to the general public as low based on available information.

items.title: World Bank warns of AI concentration risks as it lifts East Asia and Pacific growth outlook to 4.5%
items.description: The World Bank now expects the region to grow 4.5% this year, but flagged that trade growth outside AI-related goods has been "weak or negative."

items.title: Pentagon says Trump approves Army firing squad execution of Fort Hood killer Nidal Hasan
items.description: Former Army Maj. Nidal Hassan was sentenced to death after a court-martial that convicted him of killing 13 and wounding 32 others at an Army base in Texas.

items.title: Russian gold floods Hong Kong as Western sanctions redraw bullion trade
items.description: The surge underscores how Russia's gold trade has been rerouted after its invasion of Ukraine in 2022 shut its producers out of major Western markets.

items.title: Trump says MAGA Inc. PAC will pay for controversial TV ads that government funded
items.description: The New York Times reported "Trump personally instructed his budget director to use taxpayer money for TV ads praising him and his presidency."

Could not retrieve a transcript for the video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cud70hJOS-o! This is most likely caused by:

YouTube is blocking requests from your IP. This usually is due to one of the following reasons:
- You have done too many requests and your IP has been blocked by YouTube
- You are doing requests from an IP belonging to a cloud provider (like AWS, Google Cloud Platform, Azure, etc.). Unfortunately, most IPs from cloud providers are blocked by YouTube.

There are two things you can do to work around this:
1. Use proxies to hide your IP address, as explained in the "Working around IP bans" section of the README (https://github.com/jdepoix/youtube-transcript-api?tab=readme-ov-file#working-around-ip-bans-requestblocked-or-ipblocked-exception).
2. (NOT RECOMMENDED) If you authenticate your requests using cookies, you will be able to continue doing requests for a while. However, YouTube will eventually permanently ban the account that you have used to authenticate with! So only do this if you don't mind your account being banned!

If you are sure that the described cause is not responsible for this error and that a transcript should be retrievable, please create an issue at https://github.com/jdepoix/youtube-transcript-api/issues. Please add which version of youtube_transcript_api you are using and provide the information needed to replicate the error. Also make sure that there are no open issues which already describe your problem!

items.description: The symphony announced last week that it was pausing the rest of the season after disclosing financial trouble. The concerts are back on now, thanks to a tech company gift.

items.title: High Interest Rates Aren’t Slowing the A.I. Boom. That’s a Problem for the Fed.
items.description: Rising borrowing costs are taking a toll on households and businesses. But they are doing little to dampen enthusiasm for investments in A.I. infrastructure, which are contributing to inflation.

items.title: Texas Pediatricians Face Paxton Investigations for Vaccinating Children
items.description: Ken Paxton, the Texas attorney general and Republican Senate candidate, has alleged a sprawling profit-driven conspiracy. Pediatricians say the accusations are an attempt at intimidation.

items.title: War With Iran Is Forcing the World to Reckon With Geography’s Power
